title: 3D Hydrogel Scaffolds for Articular Chondrocyte Culture and Cartilage Generation
protocol: Obtain cartilage from tissue discarded during total knee arthroplasty.
Dissect the cartilage as previously described.
Visually select smooth surfaces on medial or lateral femoral condyles for biopsy.
Make incisions with a scalpel at the surface of selected areas to remove 4-5 mm cartilage biopsies without affecting subchondral bone.
Isolate chondrocytes from extracellular matrix by enzymatic dissociation using O/N treatment with purified collagenase.
Use a 1:1 ratio of Collagenase II (125 U/ml) and Collagenase IV (160 U/ml) in chondrocyte growth media at 37 °C.
Filter the digested tissue containing the dissociated cells through a 70 μm pore size Nylon mesh the following day.
Wash the filtered tissue two times with 20 ml of DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600 x g for 5 min.
Plate isolated chondrocytes at a density of 1 x 10^6 cells/60 mm culture dish after resuspension in DMEM/F12 supplemented with 10% FBS, 25 μg/ml ascorbate, 2 mM L-glutamine, and antimicrobials.
Keep plates at 37 °C to maintain primary chondrocyte cultures as a high-density monolayer prior to encapsulation in biomimetic hydrogels.
Dissolve 1.952 g of MES and 5.84 g of NaCl in 200 ml of deionized water.
Dissolve 5 g of chondroitin sulfate sodium salt in the buffered solution.
Add 0.532 g (4.62 mmol) N-hydroxysuccinimide and 1.771 g (9.24 mmol) EDC to the solution.
Stir the mixture for 5 min.
Add 0.765 g (4.62 mmol) AEMA to the reaction mixture.
Maintain the reaction at room temperature for 24 hours.
Purify the mixture by dialysis against deionized water using dialysis tubing with a molecular weight cutoff of 12-14 kDa.
Filter the purified solution through a 0.22 μm filter.
Place the open tubes containing the solution in a desiccator and evacuate overnight to remove moisture.
Store the dissolved polymer at -20°C protected from light and moisture.
Autoclave the PCR film and cylindrical rods.
Sterilize the custom-made cylindrical gel mold by submersion in 0.2 µm filtered 70% ethanol under UV light.
Seal the bottom of the gel mold with autoclaved PCR film without air bubbles or gaps.
Dissociate high-density chondrocyte monolayer with overnight treatment in Collagenase II and Collagenase IV solution.
Use 125 U/ml of Collagenase II and 160 U/ml of Collagenase VI each in chondrocyte growth media at 37 °C.
Take a 50 ml tube and add 5% weight/volume (w/v) poly(ethylene glycol diacrylate) (PEGDA, MW=5,000 g/mole).
Add 3% w/v chondroitin sulfate-methacrylate (CS-MA) to the tube.
Add 0.05% w/v photoinitiator in DPBS to the tube.
Vortex the tube to mix the solution thoroughly.
Protect the tube from light.
Collect dissociated cells in a 50 ml Falcon tube.
Count and centrifuge collected cells at 460 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate all media from the cells tube.
Add mixed gel material to re-suspend cells at a density of 15×10^6 cells/ml.
Mix thoroughly while avoiding air bubble formation.
Pipette 72 µl of cell-hydrogel suspension or hydrogel alone into the custom-made cylindrical gel mold.
Induce gelation through exposure to UV light (365 nm wavelength) at 3 mW/m² for 5 min.
Measure the intensity of the UV light with a UV intensity meter.
Adjust UV light intensity by changing the distance between the source and the hydrogel scaffold during gelation.
Prepare acellular hydrogel solution as negative controls for biochemical and mechanical testing.
Cut the film using a scalpel to facilitate peel-off.
Carefully remove the film from the gel mold.
Push out the gel into a 6 well plate with 5 ml of sterile DPBS to wash off unpolymerized gel and loose cells.
Transfer washed hydrogels into 24 well plates containing 1.5 ml of chondrocyte growth media per well using a disposable spatula.
Assess cell viability by live-dead staining 24 hours post-encapsulation using a viability/cytotoxicity kit.
Culture the cell-laden hydrogels and empty hydrogels for 3-6 weeks, changing to fresh chondrocyte growth media every 2 days before harvesting for analyses.
Aspirate the media from the cell-laden and empty control hydrogels.
Add sterile PBS 1X to the cell-laden and empty control hydrogels.
Transfer each hydrogel to a clean 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube using a sterile spatula.
Add 250 µl of Tri-reagent to each Eppendorf tube.
Isolate RNA following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Quantify the isolated RNA.
Use 1 µg of RNA from each sample for reverse transcription into cDNA.
Perform reversed transcription using the High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit.
For quantitative PCR, use TaqMan Gene Expression Arrays to examine gene expression levels.
Normalize gene expression levels internally to GAPDH.
Incubate at 50 °C for 2 minutes to inactivate previous amplicons with uracil-DNA glycosylase.
Incubate at 95 °C for 10 minutes to activate the Taq polymerase.
Perform forty cycles of PCR, consisting of 15 seconds at 95 °C and 1 minute at 60 °C.
Carefully aspirate the media from cell-hydrogel constructs.
Put sterile PBS 1X on the cell-laden and empty control hydrogels for biochemical analyses.
Weigh an empty tube.
Place the hydrogel inside after blotting it on tissue paper.
Record the weight or wet weight of the hydrogels.
Freeze each hydrogel at -20 °C in a separate 1.5 ml eppendorf tube for enzymatic digestion.
Prepare the papainase solution for enzymatic digestion of the hydrogels.
Weigh out 7.1 g of Sodium phosphate dibasic (Na2HPO4) and 1.6 g of Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium salt (EDTA-Na2).
Dissolve in 500 ml of dH2O, adjust the pH to 6.5.
Filter the purified solution through a 0.22 mm filter.
Dissolve 0.035 g of L-cysteine in 20 ml of PBE buffer.
Filter the solution and add 100 µl of sterile papain enzyme.
Take tubes from -20 °C and add 300 μl of the ready papain solution to the frozen hydrogels.
Crush the gel with a mortar and pestle and mix it well.
Bring the volume to 500 µl with additional papain solution.
Incubate at 60 °C for 16 hr.
Measure the DNA content using the Picogreen assay with Lambda phage DNA as standard following manufacturer’s protocol.
Quantify the sulfated-GAG content using the 1,9-dimethylmethylene blue (DMMB) dye-binding assay with shark chondroitin sulfate as standard.
Perform unconfined compression tests using an Instron 5944 testing system fitted with a 10 N load cell.
Submerge the specimens in a PBS bath at room temperature.
Compress the specimens at a rate of 1% strain per second to a maximum strain of 15%.
Create stress vs. strain curves.
Curve fit using a third order polynomial equation.
Determine the compressive tangent modulus from the curve fit equation at strain values of 15%.
